chunks: 1941 - Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurārah, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام what is the limit of the illness in which the fasting person breaks the fast and leaves the salat (prayer) from standing, so he said:
"Rather, man is a witness against himself."
And he knows best what he is able to bear.

key_terms.بَصِيرَةٌ: clear awareness or testimony regarding oneself
key_terms.يُطِيقُهُ: what one is capable of bearing
key_terms.يُفْطِرُ: breaks the fast due to a valid excuse
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةَ: the salat (prayer), here in relation to praying while standing or sitting
key_terms.ٱلْمَرَضِ: illness that may justify legal concessions

ai.seo_question: What level of illness allows a person to break the fast or pray sitting instead of standing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal principle for illness-related concessions in fasting and salat (prayer): the person himself is most aware of his own condition and capacity. By citing the Quran, the Imam عليه السلام indicates that the measure of hardship here is tied to what one can truly bear.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1941 - Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurara, who said:

"I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about the extent of illness that permits a fasting person to break their fast and to pray sitting instead of standing.
Imam (as) said: 'Indeed, man is a witness over himself' (Surah Al-Qiyamah 75:14), and he knows best what he can bear."
